sentences.text: G. wagneri was the first chondrichthyan recognized from the Solnhofen Limestone.
G. elongata was among the earliest named distinct genus and species of Jurassic sharks.
The holotype specimens of both G. elongata and G. wagneri are kept at the Bayerische Staatssammlung für Paläontologie und Geologie.
Some vertebrae later taken from the G. elongata holotype may have been transferred to the University of Wrocław.
The vertebrae of G. elongata display a tectospondylic calcification pattern comparable to that seen in Pseudorhina species and Notidanoides muensteri.
Dermal denticles of Georgaello resemble morphotypes recorded in other Jurassic sharks such as Asterodermus platypterus and Pseudorhina alifera.
Georgaello is placed in the class Chondrichthyes and the infraclass Neoselachii.
The type species of the genus is Georgaello elongata, which was first described by Münster in 1836.
A second species, Georgaello wagneri, was described by Agassiz in 1843.
Both species are known from Germany.
Georgaello lived during the Late Jurassic in the region that is now Germany.
Because the holotypes lack complete illustrations and their anatomy remains uncertain, the genus cannot be assigned to any group more specific than Neoselachii.
